final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 forms the catalytic Schiff base with the PLP cofactor; mutating Lys119 to alanine directly abolishes catalytic activity.
Replacing catalytic Lys119 with negatively charged glutamate prevents PLP binding and severely inactivates the enzyme.
Cys52 acts as an axial heme ligand; mutation to alanine disrupts heme coordination and leads to severe loss of CBS activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top 3 candidates finalized targeting critical catalytic and cofactor-binding residues.

history.rationale: K119 is the catalytic Schiff base lysine required for pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP) cofactor binding; alanine substitution completely prevents PLP attachment and abolishes catalytic activity.
K119 forms the essential Schiff base with PLP cofactor. Mutating Lys119 to Ala directly abolishes catalytic activity.
Substituting the catalytic Schiff base lysine K119 with glutamate introduces a negative charge that abolishes PLP cofactor binding and inactivates CBS.
Replacing catalytic Lys119 with negatively charged Glu severely disrupts PLP binding and inactivates the enzyme.
C52 is an essential axial thiolate ligand for the N-terminal heme iron; loss of heme ligation disrupts native folding and catalytic function.
Cys52 serves as an axial heme ligand. Mutation to Ala impairs heme coordination and inactivates CBS.
H65 serves as the histidine axial ligand coordinating the heme cofactor; removing this ligand impairs heme binding and severely reduces enzyme activity.
His65 is the opposite axial heme ligand. Substitution with Ala destroys heme binding and catalytic function.
Replacing the axial thiolate cysteine 52 with serine disrupts heme ligation, destabilizing the protein and abolishing activity.
Replacing Cys52 with Ser disrupts iron-thiolate ligation, leading to loss of enzyme function.
T191M is a classic pathogenic homocystinuria mutation in the catalytic domain that severely disrupts substrate positioning and enzymatic function.
T191M is a well-studied disease mutation that impairs active site conformation and causes severe loss-of-function.
S147 lies within the highly conserved active-site loop (PTSGNT) near the PLP cofactor; mutation to alanine disrupts catalytic hydrogen bonding networks.
Ser147 resides in the active site loop interacting with PLP; mutation to Ala reduces catalytic efficiency.
T150 is part of the conserved PTSGNT active-site loop; substitution eliminates key polar contacts required for efficient substrate conversion.
Thr150 stabilizes the active site loop geometry; alanine substitution weakens PLP binding and activity.
